source.text: Ἐν ἔτει δὲ πεντεκαιδεκάτῳ τῆς ἡγεμονίας Τιβερίου Καίσαρος, ἡγεμονεύοντος Ποντίου Πιλάτου τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Γαλιλαίας Ἡρῴδου, Φιλίππου δὲ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Ἰτουραίας καὶ Τραχωνίτιδος χώρας, καὶ Λυσανίου τῆς Ἀβιληνῆς τετρααρχοῦντος, ἐπὶ ἀρχιερέως Ἅννα καὶ Καϊάφα, ἐγένετο ῥῆμα θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν Ζαχαρίου υἱὸν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.

records.literal_gloss: In year then fifteenth of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, governing Pontius Pilate of the Judea, and being tetrarch of the Galilee Herod, Philip and the brother of him being tetrarch of the Ituraea and Trachonitis region, and Lysanias of the Abilene being tetrarch, \v 2 in the time of high priest Annas and Caiaphas, came word of God upon John the of Zechariah son in the wilderness.

en.L: In [the] fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governing Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene, \v 2 in the time of [the] high priest Annas and Caiaphas, [the] word of God came upon John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
en.B: It was the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar. Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea; Herod ruled Galilee as tetrarch, his brother Philip ruled the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias ruled Abilene. \v 2 Annas and Caiaphas held the high priesthood. In that year the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
en.R: Tiberius Caesar had been the Roman emperor for almost fifteen years. Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea. Herod ruled Galilee, and his brother Philip ruled the lands of Ituraea and Trachonitis. Lysanias ruled Abilene. \v 2 Annas and Caiaphas were the high priests. At that time God spoke {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} message to John, the son of Zechariah, in the desert.

es.L: En [el] año decimoquinto del gobierno de Tiberio César, cuando Poncio Pilato gobernaba Judea, y Herodes era tetrarca de Galilea, y su hermano Felipe tetrarca de la región de Iturea y Traconite, y Lisanias tetrarca de Abilene, \v 2 bajo [el] sumo sacerdote Anás y Caifás, vino [la] palabra de Dios sobre Juan, el hijo de Zacarías, en el desierto.
es.B: Era el año quince del reinado de Tiberio César. Poncio Pilato era gobernador de Judea; Herodes gobernaba Galilea como tetrarca; su hermano Felipe gobernaba la región de Iturea y Traconite, y Lisanias gobernaba Abilene. \v 2 Anás y Caifás ocupaban el sumo sacerdocio. En ese año la palabra de Dios vino a Juan, hijo de Zacarías, en el desierto.
es.R: Tiberio César llevaba casi quince años como emperador de Roma. Poncio Pilato era el gobernador romano de Judea. Herodes gobernaba Galilea, y su hermano Felipe gobernaba las tierras de Iturea y Traconite. Lisanias gobernaba Abilene. \v 2 Anás y Caifás eran los sumos sacerdotes. En ese tiempo Dios le comunicó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mensaje a Juan, el hijo de Zacarías, en el desierto.

fr.L: En la quinzième année du règne de Tibère César, Ponce Pilate étant gouverneur de la Judée, Hérode tétrarque de la Galilée, Philippe son frère tétrarque du pays d’Iturée et de Trachonitide, et Lysanias tétrarque d’Abilène, \v 2 au temps du grand prêtre Anne et de Caïphe, la parole de Dieu vint sur Jean, le fils de Zacharie, dans le désert.
fr.B: C’était la quinzième année du règne de Tibère César. Ponce Pilate était gouverneur de la Judée ; Hérode gouvernait la Galilée comme tétrarque, son frère Philippe la région de l’Iturée et de la Trachonitide, et Lysanias l’Abilène. \v 2 Anne et Caïphe exerçaient la charge de grand prêtre. Cette année-là, la parole de Dieu vint à Jean, fils de Zacharie, qui était dans le désert.
fr.R: L’empereur romain Tibère César régnait depuis presque quinze ans. Ponce Pilate était le gouverneur romain de la Judée. Hérode gouvernait la Galilée, et son frère Philippe gouvernait les régions de l’Iturée et de la Trachonitide. Lysanias gouvernait l’Abilène. \v 2 Anne et Caïphe étaient les grands prêtres. À ce moment-là, Dieu a adressé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} message à Jean, le fils de Zacharie, dans le désert.

sw.L: Basi katika mwaka wa kumi na tano wa utawala wa Tiberio Kaisari, Pontio Pilato alipokuwa akiitawala Uyahudi, na Herode akiwa mtawala wa Galilaya, na Filipo ndugu yake mtawala wa eneo la Iturea na Trakoniti, na Lisania mtawala wa Abilene, \v 2 wakati wa kuhani mkuu Anasi na Kayafa, neno la Mungu lilikuja juu ya Yohana mwana wa Zakaria nyikani.
sw.B: Ilikuwa mwaka wa kumi na tano wa utawala wa Tiberio Kaisari. Pontio Pilato alikuwa gavana wa Uyahudi; Herode alikuwa mtawala wa Galilaya, ndugu yake Filipo alitawala eneo la Iturea na Trakoniti, na Lisania alitawala Abilene. \v 2 Anasi na Kayafa walishika ukuhani mkuu. Mwaka huo neno la Mungu lilimfikia Yohana mwana wa Zakaria huko nyikani.
sw.R: Tiberio Kaisari alikuwa ametawala kama mfalme mkuu wa Roma kwa karibu miaka kumi na tano. Pontio Pilato alikuwa mtawala wa Kirumi wa Uyahudi. Herode alitawala Galilaya, na ndugu yake Filipo alitawala nchi za Iturea na Trakoniti. Lisania alitawala Abilene. \v 2 Anasi na Kayafa walikuwa makuhani wakuu. Wakati huo Mungu alimpa Yohana, mwana wa Zakaria, ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} huko jangwani.

decisions.choice: the fifteenth year of Tiberius: about AD 28 or 29
alternatives: an exact date that all would agree on
decisions.reason: Tiberius became emperor in AD 14, after Augustus (2:1). Counting from then, the fifteenth year is AD 28-29. If Luke counted from AD 12, when Tiberius began to share rule, it would be about AD 26. Like a historian, Luke dates the event by the rulers of the time.

decisions.choice: tetrarch: a ruler of part of a kingdom, under Rome
decisions.reason: The title first meant the ruler of a quarter. Herod the Great's kingdom was divided among his sons after his death: Herod Antipas took Galilee and Perea, Philip the lands north-east of the Sea of Galilee. Archelaus, who had Judea, was removed in AD 6, and Roman governors such as Pilate (AD 26-36) took his place.

decisions.choice: the high priest Annas and Caiaphas: Caiaphas held the office, and Annas, his father-in-law, kept great power
decisions.reason: Annas was high priest from AD 6 to 15; Caiaphas, his son-in-law, from AD 18 to 36 (John 18:13). The singular "high priest" with two names reflects how Annas still held authority and the title (Acts 4:6).

decisions.choice: the word of God came upon John: the way the prophets' calls are told
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament says the word of the LORD "came" to Jeremiah and the other prophets (Jeremiah 1:1-2), with the kings of the time named first. Luke presents John as a prophet in that line.

decisions.choice: the rulers in separate sentences, then the main event
decisions.reason: The Greek piles up the rulers before the main verb. Balanced breaks the list up and gives the main event its own sentence.

decisions.choice: ruled
decisions.reason: Readable avoids the technical title.

decisions.choice: God spoke his message to John
alternatives: the word of God came upon John
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means.

decisions.choice: tetrarca (L, B); gobernaba (R)
decisions.reason: The title of a ruler of part of a kingdom under Rome (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep the Spanish form of the title; Readable says plainly that each one ruled, as the English Readable does. The same through Luke.

decisions.choice: bajo [el] sumo sacerdote Anás y Caifás
alternatives: siendo sumos sacerdotes Anás y Caifás
decisions.reason: The Greek has one high priest and two names (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the singular; Balanced speaks of the office the two held, and Readable calls them both high priests, as the English does.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 2 and the other Gospels: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative in French and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. John's preaching keeps the tenses of speech at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: le grand prêtre (L, B); les grands prêtres (R), without a hyphen
decisions.reason: As the term sheet (style guide 9) has it. "Souverain sacrificateur" is the old Protestant term and is no longer current. Readable follows the English "high priests" for the two men (m3).

decisions.choice: mtawala
decisions.reason: A tetrarch ruled part of a kingdom under Rome (meaning decision m2). Swahili has no title of its own for this, and "mfalme" (king) would claim too much, so "mtawala" (ruler) serves at every level. The same through Luke.

decisions.choice: ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}
decisions.reason: As in Matthew, Swahili spans go only on free pronouns and possessives, never on verb prefixes (alimpa, alitawala), which cannot take a capital; so Swahili has fewer spans than English through Luke.

records.literal_gloss: And he came into all the region around of the Jordan proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins, \v 4 as it is written in book of words of Isaiah the prophet, Voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of [the] Lord, straight make the paths of him;

en.L: And he went into all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for [the] forgiveness of sins, \v 4 as it is written in [the] book of [the] words of Isaiah the prophet, "[The] voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of [the] Lord; make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight.'
en.B: He went through all the country around the Jordan, announcing a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins. \v 4 It was as it stands written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: "A voice is calling out in the wilderness, 'Get the road ready for the Lord, make the paths straight for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.'
en.R: John went all over the land near the Jordan River. He told people, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive you." \v 4 This happened just as the prophet Isaiah had written in his book: "Someone is shouting in the desert, 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make the path straight for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!'

es.L: Y fue por toda la región alrededor del Jordán, proclamando un bautismo de arrepentimiento para [el] perdón de pecados, \v 4 como está escrito en [el] libro de [las] palabras de Isaías el profeta: «Voz de uno que clama en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino del Señor; {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} rectas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sendas.
es.B: Recorrió toda la región del Jordán anunciando un bautismo de arrepentimiento para el perdón de los pecados. \v 4 Así estaba escrito en el libro de las palabras del profeta Isaías: «Una voz grita en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino para el Señor, {{plural_you:abran|abrid}} sendas rectas para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Juan recorrió toda la tierra cercana al río Jordán. Le decía a la gente: «{{plural_you:Apártense de sus|Apartaos de vuestros}} pecados y {{plural_you:bautícense|bautizaos}}, y Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} perdonará». \v 4 Así ocurrió lo que el profeta Isaías había escrito en su libro: «Alguien grita en el desierto: “¡{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino para el Señor! ¡{{plural_you:Abran|Abrid}} un sendero recto para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!

fr.L: Et il alla dans toute la région autour du Jourdain, proclamant un baptême de repentance pour le pardon des péchés, \v 4 comme il est écrit dans le livre des paroles d’Isaïe le prophète : « [La] voix de quelqu’un qui crie dans le désert : “Préparez le chemin du Seigneur, rendez droits {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sentiers.
fr.B: Il parcourut toute la région du Jourdain en proclamant un baptême de repentance pour le pardon des péchés. \v 4 Il en fut ainsi comme il est écrit dans le livre des paroles du prophète Isaïe : « Une voix crie dans le désert : “Préparez la route du Seigneur, tracez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} des sentiers droits.
fr.R: Jean est allé partout dans la région du fleuve Jourdain. Il disait aux gens : « Détournez-vous de vos péchés et faites-vous baptiser, et Dieu vous pardonnera. » \v 4 Cela s’est passé comme le prophète Isaïe l’avait écrit dans son livre : « Quelqu’un crie dans le désert : “Préparez la route pour le Seigneur ! Faites-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un chemin bien droit !

sw.L: Naye alikwenda katika eneo lote linalozunguka Yordani, akitangaza ubatizo wa toba kwa ajili ya msamaha wa dhambi, \v 4 kama ilivyoandikwa katika kitabu cha maneno ya Isaya nabii, "Sauti ya mtu anayepaza sauti nyikani: 'Iandaeni njia ya Bwana, yafanyeni mapito {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yanyooke;
sw.B: Alipita katika nchi yote iliyo kando ya Yordani, akitangaza ubatizo wa toba ili watu wasamehewe dhambi zao. \v 4 Ilikuwa kama ilivyoandikwa katika kitabu cha maneno ya nabii Isaya: "Sauti inaita nyikani: 'Mtengenezeeni Bwana barabara, nyoosheni mapito kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}};
sw.R: Yohana alikwenda kila mahali katika nchi iliyo karibu na mto Yordani. Aliwaambia watu, "Acheni dhambi zenu mbatizwe, na Mungu atawasamehe." \v 4 Hili lilitokea kama nabii Isaya alivyoandika katika kitabu chake: "Mtu anapiga kelele jangwani: 'Mtengenezeeni Bwana barabara! Nyoosheni njia kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}!

decisions.choice: a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins: being washed in water as a sign of turning back to God, who forgives
alternatives: a washing that itself removes sin
decisions.reason: Repentance is a change of mind and life, a turning back to God (1:16-17). The baptism expresses that turning, and forgiveness is God's answer to it (compare Acts 2:38).

decisions.choice: a voice crying in the wilderness: Isaiah 40:3-5, quoted from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Isaiah announced God's coming to bring his exiled people home, with a road prepared through the desert. All four Gospels apply the words to John. "The Lord" stands for the divine name in the Hebrew; Isaiah has "our God" where Luke has "his paths".

decisions.choice: in the wilderness: the voice cries in the wilderness
alternatives: prepare in the wilderness the way of the Lord
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Isaiah 40:3 "in the wilderness" goes with "prepare". In the Greek, which Luke quotes, it can go with the voice, and John is in the wilderness (3:2).

decisions.choice: He told people, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive you."
alternatives: proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins
decisions.reason: Readable turns the dense phrase into what John said.

decisions.choice: the road (B, R); the way (L)
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the picture is a road built for a king; Balanced and Readable keep the picture.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks inside the quotation for the voice's words
decisions.reason: The quotation from Isaiah includes the words the voice cries. The quotation runs on to the end of 3:6.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}}
decisions.reason: The voice speaks to many, so every plural "you" takes the reader setting: "ustedes" (Latin America, the default) or "vosotros" (Spain). English has no such choice. The same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: bautismo de arrepentimiento (L, B); «Apártense de sus pecados y bautícense» (R)
decisions.reason: "Arrepentimiento" is the word for repentance through Luke (meaning decision m1). Readable puts John's message in his own words, turning from sin and being baptized, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: la repentance (L, B); se détourner de ses péchés (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet (style guide 9) has it: "se repentir, la repentance" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says it in plain words, as the English Readable does (m1).

decisions.choice: « » for the quotation from Isaiah, “ ” for the voice's words inside it
decisions.reason: French marks a quotation inside a quotation with “ ”, as the English uses single marks. Both close at the end of 3:6.

decisions.choice: ubatizo wa toba (L, B); Acheni dhambi zenu mbatizwe (R)
decisions.reason: "Toba" is the word for repentance through Luke (meaning decision m1). Readable puts John's message in his own words, turning from sin and being baptized, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: nyika (L, B); jangwa (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is open, empty country, not only sand desert. "Nyika" is the uninhabited bush; Readable uses the more common "jangwa", as the English Readable says "desert". The same through Luke.

records.literal_gloss: Every valley will be filled and every mountain and hill will be made low, and will be the crooked into straight and the rough into ways smooth;

en.L: Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be made low, and the crooked [places] will become straight, and the rough [places] smooth roads,
en.B: Every valley will be filled in, and every mountain and hill brought low; the winding roads will be made straight, and the rough roads level,
en.R: Every valley will be filled up. Every mountain and hill will be made flat. The crooked roads will be made straight, and the rough roads will be made smooth.

decisions.choice: valleys filled and mountains made low: the way prepared for God's coming, and the proud brought down
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the picture is of a highway built for a king's arrival. Luke has already sung of God bringing down the mighty and lifting up the lowly (1:52); the picture fits John's call to change.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all people
decisions.reason: "Flesh" in Hebrew speech means human beings in their weakness. Luke alone continues the quotation to this line: God's salvation is for all peoples (2:30-32).

decisions.choice: the salvation of God: God's saving work
decisions.reason: The noun is the one Simeon used (2:30).

decisions.choice: all people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying therefore to the coming out crowds to be baptized by him, Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

en.L: So he was saying to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, "Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
en.B: So John would say to the crowds who came out to be baptized by him, "You children of snakes! Who told you to run from the anger that is coming?
en.R: Crowds of people came out to be baptized by John. He said to them, "You are like a family of poisonous snakes! Who warned you to escape from God's coming anger?

es.L: Decía, pues, a las multitudes que salían para ser bautizadas por él: «¡Crías de víboras! ¿Quién {{plural_you:les|os}} advirtió que {{plural_you:huyeran|huyerais}} de la ira venidera?
es.B: Así que Juan les decía a las multitudes que salían para que él las bautizara: «¡Hijos de serpientes! ¿Quién {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo que {{plural_you:huyeran|huyerais}} de la ira que viene?
es.R: Mucha gente salía para que Juan la bautizara. Él les decía: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} como una familia de serpientes venenosas! ¿Quién {{plural_you:les|os}} avisó que {{plural_you:escaparan|escaparais}} de la ira de Dios que se acerca?

fr.L: Il disait donc aux foules qui sortaient pour être baptisées par lui : « Progéniture de vipères, qui vous a avertis de fuir la colère qui vient ?
fr.B: Jean disait donc aux foules qui venaient se faire baptiser par lui : « Enfants de serpents ! Qui vous a dit d’échapper à la colère qui approche ?
fr.R: Des foules de gens venaient pour être baptisées par Jean. Il leur disait : « Vous êtes comme une famille de serpents venimeux ! Qui vous a avertis de fuir la colère de Dieu qui va venir ?

sw.L: Basi alikuwa akiwaambia makutano waliokuwa wakitoka kubatizwa naye, "Ninyi uzao wa nyoka wenye sumu! Ni nani aliyewaonya kukimbia ghadhabu ijayo?
sw.B: Basi Yohana alikuwa akiwaambia makundi ya watu waliokuja ili awabatize, "Ninyi watoto wa nyoka! Ni nani aliyewaambia mkimbie ghadhabu inayokuja?
sw.R: Makundi ya watu yalikuja ili Yohana awabatize. Aliwaambia, "Ninyi ni kama jamaa ya nyoka wenye sumu! Ni nani aliyewaonya mwiepuke hasira ya Mungu inayokuja?

decisions.choice: offspring of vipers: people as dangerous and deceitful as snakes, and fleeing like them
decisions.reason: Snakes flee before a fire in the desert scrub. John asks whether they come only to escape the coming judgment, without changing their lives (3:8).

decisions.choice: the coming wrath: God's judgment at the coming of his day
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of the day of the LORD as a day of wrath (Zephaniah 1:15; Malachi 4:1). John announces that it is near (3:9, 17).

decisions.choice: he was saying: he said this often
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense shows a typical message, spoken to the crowds again and again.

decisions.choice: children of snakes (B); a family of poisonous snakes (R)
decisions.reason: "Brood of vipers" is familiar but archaic. Balanced and Readable keep the insult in plain words.

decisions.choice: God's coming anger
decisions.reason: Readable names whose anger it is.

decisions.choice: Crías de víboras
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 3:7: the Greek word is the young of an animal (meaning decision m1), and "crías" says that plainly. Balanced and Readable speak of the children or family of snakes, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Progéniture de vipères (L); Enfants de serpents (B); une famille de serpents venimeux (R)
decisions.reason: "Race de vipères" is the familiar wording, but "race" is now a loaded word in French and "engeance" is literary. Literal keeps "offspring" with "progéniture"; Balanced and Readable keep the insult in plain words, as the English does (m1).

source.text: ποιήσατε οὖν καρποὺς ἀξίους τῆς μετανοίας· καὶ μὴ ἄρξησθε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.

records.literal_gloss: Produce therefore fruits worthy of the repentance; and not begin to say in yourselves, Father we have the Abraham, I say for to you that is able the God from the stones these to raise up children to the Abraham.

en.L: Produce, then, fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say among yourselves, 'We have Abraham [as] father,' for I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.
en.B: Then bear fruit that fits your repentance. And do not start telling yourselves, 'Abraham is our father.' I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham out of these stones.
en.R: If you have really turned away from your sins, then show it by the way you live. Do not think to yourselves, 'We belong to Abraham's family, so we are safe.' I tell you, God could turn these stones into children of Abraham!

es.L: {{plural_you:Produzcan|Producid}}, pues, frutos dignos del arrepentimiento, y no {{plural_you:comiencen|comencéis}} a decir para {{plural_you:sí mismos|vosotros mismos}}: “Tenemos a Abraham [por] padre”, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que Dios puede de estas piedras levantar hijos a Abraham.
es.B: {{plural_you:Den|Dad}}, entonces, el fruto que corresponde a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} arrepentimiento. Y no {{plural_you:empiecen a decirse|empecéis a deciros}}: “Abraham es nuestro padre”. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que Dios puede sacar de estas piedras hijos para Abraham.
es.R: Si de verdad {{plural_you:se han apartado|os habéis apartado}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados, {{plural_you:demuéstrenlo|demostradlo}} con {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de vivir. No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}}: “Somos de la familia de Abraham, así que estamos a salvo”. ¡{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que Dios podría convertir estas piedras en hijos de Abraham!

fr.L: Portez donc des fruits dignes de la repentance, et n’allez pas vous dire en vous-mêmes : “Abraham, nous l’avons pour père”, car je vous le dis : Dieu est capable, à partir de ces pierres, de faire surgir des enfants pour Abraham.
fr.B: Que votre vie porte donc des fruits qui conviennent à votre repentance. Et ne commencez pas à vous dire : “Abraham est notre père.” Je vous le dis, de ces pierres Dieu peut faire naître des enfants pour Abraham.
fr.R: Si vous vous êtes vraiment détournés de vos péchés, montrez-le par votre manière de vivre. Ne pensez pas : “Nous faisons partie de la famille d’Abraham, alors nous ne risquons rien.” Je vous le dis, Dieu pourrait changer ces pierres en enfants d’Abraham !

sw.L: Basi zaeni matunda yanayostahili toba, wala msianze kusema ndani yenu, 'Tuna Ibrahimu [kuwa] baba,' kwa maana nawaambia kwamba Mungu anaweza kutoka katika mawe haya kuinua watoto kwa ajili ya Ibrahimu.
sw.B: Basi zaeni matunda yanayolingana na toba yenu. Wala msianze kujiambia, 'Ibrahimu ni baba yetu.' Nawaambia, Mungu anaweza kuinua watoto wa Ibrahimu kutoka katika mawe haya.
sw.R: Kama kweli mmeacha dhambi zenu, onyesheni hivyo kwa jinsi mnavyoishi. Msifikiri moyoni, 'Sisi ni wa jamaa ya Ibrahimu, kwa hiyo tuko salama.' Nawaambia, Mungu angeweza kuyageuza mawe haya kuwa watoto wa Ibrahimu!

decisions.choice: fruits worthy of repentance: a changed life that shows the turning is real
decisions.reason: Fruit is what a life produces. 3:10-14 gives examples.

decisions.choice: we have Abraham as father: descent from Abraham as a guarantee of safety
alternatives: a claim to be like Abraham
decisions.reason: Some trusted that as Abraham's descendants they belonged to God's people whatever they did (compare John 8:33, 39). John says descent is no protection.

decisions.choice: God can raise children for Abraham from these stones: God does not depend on them to keep his promise
alternatives: a literal miracle that John expects
decisions.reason: In Hebrew and Aramaic the words for "sons" and "stones" sound alike, which may lie behind the saying. Abraham himself was called the rock from which Israel was cut (Isaiah 51:1-2).

decisions.choice: show it by the way you live
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

decisions.choice: so we are safe
decisions.reason: Readable says why they would make the claim, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ἤδη δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.

records.literal_gloss: Already and also the ax at the root of the trees is laid; every therefore tree not producing fruit good is cut down and into fire is thrown.

en.L: And already the ax is laid at the root of the trees; so every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into [the] fire."
en.B: The ax is already lying at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire."
en.R: God is ready to judge, like a man who has his ax ready to cut down trees. Every tree that does not grow good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."

es.L: Y ya también el hacha está puesta junto a la raíz de los árboles; así que todo árbol que no da fruto bueno es cortado y echado al fuego».
es.B: El hacha ya está puesta a la raíz de los árboles, y todo árbol que no dé buen fruto se corta y se arroja al fuego».
es.R: Dios está listo para juzgar, como un hombre que ya tiene el hacha preparada para cortar árboles. Todo árbol que no dé buen fruto será cortado y echado al fuego».

fr.L: Et déjà la hache est posée à la racine des arbres ; donc tout arbre qui ne produit pas de bon fruit est coupé et jeté au feu. »
fr.B: La hache est déjà au pied des arbres, et tout arbre qui ne donne pas de bon fruit est abattu et jeté au feu. »
fr.R: Dieu est prêt à juger, comme un homme qui a sa hache prête pour couper les arbres. Tout arbre qui ne donne pas de bons fruits sera coupé et jeté dans le feu. »

sw.L: Na tayari shoka liko kwenye mzizi wa miti; kwa hiyo kila mti ambao hautoi tunda zuri unakatwa na kutupwa katika moto."
sw.B: Shoka limeshawekwa tayari kwenye mizizi ya miti, na mti wowote usiotoa matunda mazuri unakatwa na kutupwa motoni."
sw.R: Mungu yuko tayari kuhukumu, kama mtu aliyeshika shoka tayari kukata miti. Kila mti usiozaa matunda mazuri utakatwa na kutupwa motoni."

decisions.choice: the ax at the root: judgment is near and will be final
decisions.reason: An ax at the root does not prune; it fells the whole tree. The present tense "is cut down" speaks of the judgment as certain and near.

decisions.choice: God is ready to judge, like a man who has his ax ready
alternatives: the ax is laid at the root
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture before giving it.

source.text: Καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες· Τί οὖν ποιήσωμεν;

records.literal_gloss: And were asking him the crowds saying, What then shall we do?

en.L: And the crowds were asking him, saying, "What then should we do?"
en.B: The crowds asked him, "Then what are we to do?"
en.R: The people asked John, "What should we do?"

es.L: Y las multitudes le preguntaban, diciendo: «¿Qué, pues, debemos hacer?».
es.B: Las multitudes le preguntaban: «Entonces, ¿qué debemos hacer?».
es.R: La gente le preguntó a Juan: «¿Qué debemos hacer?».

fr.L: Et les foules l’interrogeaient, disant : « Que devrions-nous donc faire ? »
fr.B: Les foules lui demandaient : « Alors, que devons-nous faire ? »
fr.R: Les gens ont demandé à Jean : « Qu’est-ce que nous devons faire ? »

sw.L: Na makutano walikuwa wakimwuliza, wakisema, "Basi tufanye nini?"
sw.B: Makundi ya watu yalimwuliza, "Basi, tufanye nini?"

decisions.choice: what then should we do: what does repentance look like?
decisions.reason: The question takes up "fruits worthy of repentance" (3:8). John's answers are about everyday conduct.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁ ἔχων δύο χιτῶνας μεταδότω τῷ μὴ ἔχοντι, καὶ ὁ ἔχων βρώματα ὁμοίως ποιείτω.

records.literal_gloss: Answering and he was saying to them, The [one] having two tunics let him share with the [one] not having, and the [one] having food likewise let him do.

en.L: And answering he said to them, "Whoever has two tunics, let him share with the one who has none, and whoever has food, let him do likewise."
en.B: He answered them, "Whoever has two shirts must share with the person who has none, and whoever has food must do the same."
en.R: John answered, "If you have two shirts, give one to someone who has none. If you have food, share it too."

es.L: Y respondiendo, les decía: «El que tiene dos túnicas, que comparta con el que no tiene, y el que tiene comida, que haga lo mismo».
es.B: Él les respondía: «El que tenga dos camisas, que comparta con quien no tiene ninguna; y el que tenga comida, que haga lo mismo».
es.R: Juan les respondió: «Si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} dos camisas, {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} una a alguien que no tenga. Si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} comida, {{plural_you:compártanla|compartidla}} también».

fr.L: Et, répondant, il leur disait : « Celui qui a deux tuniques, qu’il partage avec celui qui n’en a pas ; et celui qui a des vivres, qu’il fasse pareillement. »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Celui qui a deux chemises doit en donner une à celui qui n’en a pas, et celui qui a de quoi manger doit faire de même. »
fr.R: Jean a répondu : « Si vous avez deux chemises, donnez-en une à quelqu’un qui n’en a pas. Si vous avez de la nourriture, partagez-la aussi. »

sw.L: Naye akijibu, alikuwa akiwaambia, "Aliye na kanzu mbili ashiriki na yule asiye nayo, na aliye na chakula afanye kadhalika."
sw.B: Aliwajibu, "Mtu mwenye mashati mawili lazima ashiriki na mtu asiye na shati, na mwenye chakula lazima afanye hivyo pia."
sw.R: Yohana aliwajibu, "Kama mna mashati mawili, mpeni mmoja mtu asiye na shati. Kama mna chakula, mgawieni pia."

decisions.choice: tunics: the long shirt worn next to the skin
decisions.reason: The tunic was the basic garment; a second was a luxury the poor could not afford.

decisions.choice: shirts
decisions.reason: "Tunic" is unfamiliar; "shirt" is the nearest everyday word for the garment worn next to the skin.

decisions.choice: kanzu (L); mashati (B, R)
decisions.reason: The garment was the long shirt worn next to the skin (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "kanzu", the long robe; Balanced and Readable say "shirts", as the English does.

source.text: ἦλθον δὲ καὶ τελῶναι βαπτισθῆναι καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσωμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Came and also tax collectors to be baptized and said to him, Teacher, what shall we do?

en.L: And tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, "Teacher, what should we do?"
en.B: Tax collectors too came to be baptized. "Teacher," they said to him, "what are we to do?"
en.R: Some tax collectors also came to be baptized. They asked John, "Teacher, what should we do?"

es.L: Vinieron también publicanos para ser bautizados, y le dijeron: «Maestro, ¿qué debemos hacer?».
es.B: También llegaron cobradores de impuestos para bautizarse. «Maestro», le dijeron, «¿qué debemos hacer?».
es.R: También vinieron algunos cobradores de impuestos para que Juan los bautizara. Le preguntaron: «Maestro, ¿qué debemos hacer?».

fr.L: Et des collecteurs d’impôts aussi vinrent pour être baptisés, et ils lui dirent : « Maître, que devrions-nous faire ? »
fr.B: Des collecteurs d’impôts vinrent aussi se faire baptiser. « Maître, lui dirent-ils, que devons-nous faire ? »
fr.R: Des collecteurs d’impôts sont aussi venus pour être baptisés. Ils ont demandé à Jean : « Maître, qu’est-ce que nous devons faire ? »

sw.L: Na walikuja pia watoza ushuru kubatizwa, wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, tufanye nini?"
sw.B: Watoza ushuru nao walikuja kubatizwa. Wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, sisi tufanye nini?"
sw.R: Baadhi ya watoza ushuru nao walikuja ili Yohana awabatize. Walimwuliza, "Mwalimu, tufanye nini?"

decisions.choice: tax collectors: Jews who collected taxes and tolls for Rome or its rulers, and were despised
decisions.reason: Tax collectors bid for the right to collect tolls and kept what they took above the set amount. They were hated as cheats and as servants of foreign rulers (5:30; 18:11; 19:7).

decisions.choice: publicanos (L); cobradores de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Publicano" is the traditional name for these men (meaning decision m1) and Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable say what they did. The same through Luke.

decisions.choice: les collecteurs d’impôts
decisions.reason: As the term sheet (style guide 9) has it: "publicains" is a church word most readers no longer understand. The word for "Teacher" is "Maître", the usual French address to a teacher of the law.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν πλέον παρὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον ὑμῖν πράσσετε.

records.literal_gloss: He and said to them, Nothing more beyond the having been ordered to you collect.

en.L: And he said to them, "Collect nothing more than what has been ordered for you."
en.B: He told them, "Take no more than the amount you have been ordered to collect."
en.R: John told them, "Do not take more money from people than you are supposed to."

es.L: Y él les dijo: «No {{plural_you:cobren|cobréis}} nada más de lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha ordenado».
es.B: Él les contestó: «No {{plural_you:cobren|cobréis}} más de lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha fijado».
es.R: Juan les dijo: «No les {{plural_you:quiten|quitéis}} a la gente más dinero del que {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} cobrar».

fr.L: Et lui leur dit : « Ne percevez rien de plus que ce qui vous a été fixé. »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Ne prélevez pas plus que le montant qu’on vous a ordonné de percevoir. »
fr.R: Jean leur a dit : « Ne prenez pas aux gens plus d’argent que ce que vous devez prendre. »

sw.L: Naye aliwaambia, "Msikusanye kitu chochote zaidi ya kile kilichoamriwa kwenu."
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Msichukue zaidi ya kiasi mlichoagizwa kukusanya."
sw.R: Yohana aliwaambia, "Msiwatoze watu fedha zaidi ya kiasi kinachotakiwa."

decisions.choice: collect nothing more: honesty in their work, not leaving it
decisions.reason: John does not tell them to leave their work, but to do it honestly.

source.text: ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ στρατευόμενοι λέγοντες· Τί ποιήσωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: Were asking and him also soldiers saying, What shall do also we?

en.L: And soldiers also were asking him, saying, "And what should we do?"
en.B: Some soldiers asked him too, "And what about us? What are we to do?"
en.R: Some soldiers asked John, "And what should we do?"

es.L: Y también le preguntaban unos soldados, diciendo: «¿Qué debemos hacer también nosotros?».
es.B: Algunos soldados también le preguntaron: «¿Y nosotros? ¿Qué debemos hacer?».
es.R: Unos soldados le preguntaron a Juan: «¿Y nosotros qué debemos hacer?».

fr.L: Et des soldats aussi l’interrogeaient, disant : « Et nous, que devrions-nous faire ? »
fr.B: Des soldats lui demandèrent aussi : « Et nous ? Que devons-nous faire ? »
fr.R: Des soldats ont demandé à Jean : « Et nous, qu’est-ce que nous devons faire ? »

sw.L: Na askari pia walikuwa wakimwuliza, wakisema, "Tufanye nini sisi pia?"
sw.B: Baadhi ya askari nao walimwuliza, "Na sisi je? Tufanye nini?"
sw.R: Askari fulani walimwuliza Yohana, "Sisi tufanye nini?"

decisions.choice: soldiers: probably men serving Herod Antipas, or guarding the tax collectors
decisions.reason: The word means men on active service. There were no Roman legions in Galilee or Judea at this time; these may be Jewish soldiers of Herod, or soldiers who protected tax collectors.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Μηδένα διασείσητε μηδὲ συκοφαντήσητε, καὶ ἀρκεῖσθε τοῖς ὀψωνίοις ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, No one extort nor accuse falsely, and be content with the wages of you.

en.L: And he said to them, "Extort from no one, and do not accuse [anyone] falsely, and be content with your wages."
en.B: He told them, "Do not shake anyone down for money or make false charges, and be satisfied with your pay."
en.R: John told them, "Do not use force or threats to take money from people. Do not lie about anyone. Be happy with the pay you get."

es.L: Y les dijo: «No {{plural_you:extorsionen|extorsionéis}} a nadie ni {{plural_you:acusen|acuséis}} falsamente, y {{plural_you:conténtense|contentaos}} con {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} paga».
es.B: Él les dijo: «No le {{plural_you:saquen|saquéis}} dinero a nadie con amenazas ni {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} denuncias falsas, y {{plural_you:confórmense|conformaos}} con {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} sueldo».
es.R: Juan les dijo: «No {{plural_you:usen|uséis}} la fuerza ni las amenazas para quitarle dinero a la gente. No {{plural_you:mientan|mintáis}} acerca de nadie. {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} contentos con la paga que {{plural_you:reciben|recibís}}».

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « N’extorquez rien à personne, et n’accusez [personne] faussement, et soyez satisfaits de votre solde. »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Ne rançonnez personne, ne portez pas de fausses accusations, et contentez-vous de ce que vous gagnez. »
fr.R: Jean leur a dit : « N’utilisez pas la force ou les menaces pour prendre de l’argent aux gens. N’accusez personne à tort. Soyez contents de la paie que vous recevez. »

sw.L: Naye aliwaambia, "Msimpokonye yeyote, wala msimsingizie [mtu yeyote], na muridhike na malipo yenu."
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Msimtishe mtu yeyote ili awape fedha, wala msiwasingizie watu mashtaka ya uongo. Ridhikeni na mshahara wenu."
sw.R: Yohana aliwaambia, "Msitumie nguvu wala vitisho kuchukua fedha za watu. Msiseme uongo juu ya mtu yeyote. Ridhikeni na malipo mnayopewa."

decisions.choice: extort: take money by violence or threats
decisions.reason: The verb means to shake, and so to shake money out of someone by intimidation.

decisions.choice: accuse falsely: get money by false charges
decisions.reason: The verb meant to extort by false accusation or blackmail. Zacchaeus uses it in 19:8.

decisions.choice: shake anyone down for money
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the Greek verb with an English idiom for extortion.

decisions.choice: Ne rançonnez personne (B)
decisions.reason: English Balanced uses an idiom ("shake down") for taking money by threats (m1). French "rançonner" is the plain word for making someone pay by force or threat, so Balanced uses it rather than the more technical "extorquer" of Literal.

decisions.choice: kumsingizia
decisions.reason: "Kusingizia" is to bring a false charge against someone, one verb as in the Greek (meaning decision m2); Balanced adds "mashtaka ya uongo" to make the charge plain, and Readable says simply not to lie about anyone, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Προσδοκῶντος δὲ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ διαλογιζομένων πάντων ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν περὶ τοῦ Ἰωάννου, μήποτε αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ χριστός, ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων πᾶσιν ὁ Ἰωάννης· Ἐγὼ μὲν ὕδατι βαπτίζω ὑμᾶς· ἔρχεται δὲ ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·

records.literal_gloss: Expecting and the people and wondering all in the hearts of them concerning the John, whether he might be the Christ, \v 16 answered saying to all the John, I indeed with water baptize you; comes but the [one] stronger than me, of whom not I am worthy to untie the strap of the sandals of him; he you will baptize in Spirit Holy and fire;

en.L: And as the people were in expectation, and all were wondering in their hearts about John, whether he might be the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 16 John answered, saying to all, "I baptize you with water, but one who is mightier than I is coming, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with [the] Holy Spirit and fire.
en.B: The people were full of expectation, and all of them were asking themselves whether John might be {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 16 John answered them all, "I baptize you with water. But someone stronger than I am is coming, and I am not fit to untie the strap of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
en.R: The people were hoping for {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} to come. They all wondered whether John might be {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 16 John answered all of them, "I baptize you with water. But someone is coming who is much greater than I am. I am not even good enough to untie {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

es.L: Y como el pueblo estaba a la expectativa, y todos se preguntaban en sus corazones acerca de Juan si acaso él sería el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, \v 16 Juan respondió, diciendo a todos: «Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizo con agua, pero viene el que es más fuerte que yo, del cual no soy digno de desatar la correa de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias. Él {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará en [el] Espíritu Santo y fuego.
es.B: El pueblo estaba lleno de expectación, y todos se preguntaban en su interior si Juan sería {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. \v 16 Juan les respondió a todos: «Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizo con agua. Pero viene alguien más fuerte que yo, y no soy digno ni de desatar la correa de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias. Él {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará con el Espíritu Santo y con fuego.
es.R: La gente esperaba la llegada {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Todos se preguntaban si Juan sería {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. \v 16 Juan les respondió a todos: «Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizo con agua. Pero viene alguien mucho más grande que yo. Yo ni siquiera merezco desatar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias. Él {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará con el Espíritu Santo y con fuego.

fr.L: Et comme le peuple était dans l’attente, et que tous se demandaient dans leur cœur, au sujet de Jean, s’il ne serait pas le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, \v 16 Jean répondit, disant à tous : « Moi, je vous baptise d’eau ; mais il vient, celui qui est plus fort que moi, dont je ne suis pas apte à délier la lanière des sandales. Lui vous baptisera dans l’Esprit Saint et le feu.
fr.B: Le peuple était dans l’attente, et tous se demandaient en eux-mêmes si Jean ne serait pas le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. \v 16 Jean leur répondit à tous : « Moi, je vous baptise avec de l’eau. Mais quelqu’un de plus fort que moi va venir, et je ne suis pas digne de dénouer la lanière de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales. Il vous baptisera avec l’Esprit Saint et avec le feu.
fr.R: Le peuple espérait la venue du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Tous se demandaient si Jean n’était pas le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. \v 16 Jean leur a répondu à tous : « Moi, je vous baptise avec de l’eau. Mais quelqu’un va venir qui est beaucoup plus grand que moi. Je ne suis même pas assez bon pour détacher {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales. Il vous baptisera avec l’Esprit Saint et avec le feu.

sw.L: Na watu walipokuwa wakitazamia, na wote wakijiuliza mioyoni mwao kuhusu Yohana, kama huenda yeye ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, \v 16 Yohana alijibu, akiwaambia wote, "Mimi nawabatiza ninyi kwa maji, lakini anakuja aliye na nguvu kuliko mimi, ambaye sifai kufungua kamba ya ndara {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Yeye atawabatiza katika Roho Mtakatifu na moto.
sw.B: Watu walikuwa wakitazamia kwa hamu, na wote walijiuliza mioyoni mwao kama huenda Yohana ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 16 Yohana aliwajibu wote, "Mimi nawabatiza kwa maji. Lakini anakuja mwenye nguvu kuliko mimi, nami sifai hata kufungua kamba za ndara {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Yeye atawabatiza kwa Roho Mtakatifu na moto.
sw.R: Watu walikuwa wakimtazamia {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} aje. Wote walijiuliza kama huenda Yohana ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 16 Yohana aliwajibu wote, "Mimi nawabatiza kwa maji. Lakini anakuja mtu aliye mkuu sana kuliko mimi. Mimi sistahili hata kufungua ndara {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Yeye atawabatiza kwa Roho Mtakatifu na moto.

decisions.choice: the people were in expectation: hoping for the Messiah
decisions.reason: Luke has shown Israel waiting for God's consolation and redemption (2:25, 38).

decisions.choice: untie the strap of his sandals: the lowest task of a slave
decisions.reason: Untying a master's sandals was a slave's task. John says he is not worthy even to be the coming one's slave.

decisions.choice: baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire: pour out the Spirit, and bring judgment and cleansing
alternatives: fire as a second name for the Spirit only
decisions.reason: In 3:17 fire is judgment; in Acts 2:3-4 the Spirit comes with tongues of fire. Fire can purify as well as destroy (Malachi 3:2-3). The one coming will either cleanse or destroy, depending on how people respond.

decisions.choice: mightier than I: the coming one, greater in power and rank
decisions.reason: John does not name him. Luke's readers know it is Jesus (3:21-22).

decisions.choice: not fit (B); not even good enough (R)
decisions.reason: "Worthy" is church language; the plain sense is "good enough".

decisions.choice: la correa de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "whose sandals" and has no span there. Spanish keeps the Greek "his" after "del cual", so that "sus" takes the deity_pronoun span, as at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: apte (L); digne (B); assez bon (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:7: the word means fit or sufficient for a task. Literal keeps that sense with "apte"; "je ne suis pas digne de" is the natural French for being unfit even for a lowly service, so Balanced uses it; Readable says "good enough", as the English does.

decisions.choice: ndara
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 3:11: "viatu" now suggests shoes; "ndara" are open sandals tied to the foot, as the Greek word means. Untying them was a slave's task (meaning decision m2).

source.text: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ διακαθᾶραι τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συναγαγεῖν τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην αὐτοῦ, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Of whom the winnowing fork in the hand of him to clear the threshing floor of him and to gather the wheat into the barn of him, the but chaff he will burn up with fire unquenchable.

en.L: His winnowing fork [is] in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, to clean out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} threshing floor and to gather the wheat into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} barn, but the chaff {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burn up with unquenchable fire."
en.B: His winnowing fork is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, to clear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} threshing floor and to gather the wheat into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} barn. But the chaff {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burn in a fire that never goes out."
en.R: He is like a farmer who has come to clean out the place where he separates the wheat from the chaff. His fork is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand. He will store the good wheat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} barn, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burn up the chaff in a fire that cannot be put out."

es.L: Su horquilla de aventar [está] en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano, para limpiar a fondo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} era y recoger el trigo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} granero, pero la paja la quemará con fuego inextinguible».
es.B: Ya tiene en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano la horquilla de aventar para limpiar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} era y recoger el trigo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} granero. Pero la paja la quemará en un fuego que nunca se apaga».
es.R: Él es como un campesino que ha venido a limpiar el lugar donde se separa el trigo de la paja. Tiene la horquilla en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano. Guardará el buen trigo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} granero, pero quemará la paja en un fuego que no se puede apagar».

fr.L: Sa fourche à vanner [est] dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main, pour nettoyer {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} aire et pour amasser le blé dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} grenier, mais la paille, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la brûlera dans un feu inextinguible. »
fr.B: Il a {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fourche à vanner à la main, pour nettoyer {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} aire de battage et rassembler le blé dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} grenier. Mais la paille, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la brûlera dans un feu qui ne s’éteint jamais. »
fr.R: Il est comme un paysan qui est venu nettoyer l’endroit où il sépare le blé de la paille. Il a {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fourche à la main. Il mettra le bon blé dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} grenier, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} brûlera la paille dans un feu qu’on ne peut pas éteindre. »

sw.L: Chombo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} cha kupepetea kiko mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, ili kuusafisha kabisa uwanja {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kupuria na kuiweka ngano ghalani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, lakini makapi atayachoma kwa moto usioweza kuzimwa."
sw.B: Ameshika mkononi chombo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} cha kupepetea, ili kusafisha uwanja {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kupuria na kuhifadhi ngano ghalani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Lakini makapi atayachoma kwa moto ambao hauzimiki kamwe."
sw.R: Yeye ni kama mkulima aliyekuja kusafisha uwanja ambapo ngano hutenganishwa na makapi. Chombo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} cha kupepetea kiko mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Ataiweka ngano nzuri ghalani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, lakini makapi atayachoma kwa moto usioweza kuzimwa."

decisions.choice: winnowing fork, threshing floor: separating grain from chaff
decisions.reason: After threshing, a farmer tossed the grain into the wind with a fork or shovel. The heavy grain fell back; the wind blew the light chaff away, and it was burned. The coming one will separate people as a farmer separates wheat from chaff.

decisions.choice: unquenchable fire: judgment that cannot be stopped
decisions.reason: The fire that is never put out is a picture of final judgment (Isaiah 66:24; Mark 9:43-48).

decisions.choice: He is like a farmer who has come to clean out the place where he separates the wheat from the chaff
alternatives: his winnowing fork is in his hand to clear his threshing floor
decisions.reason: Readable explains the farm work before naming the tools. The farmer of the comparison is not given a deity_pronoun span; the coming one is.

decisions.choice: horquilla de aventar
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 3:12: the tool is a wooden fork for tossing threshed grain into the wind (meaning decision m1). "Aventador" and "bieldo" are not known everywhere; "horquilla de aventar" says what it is.

decisions.choice: la quemará, with no span
decisions.reason: The English has a span on "he" before "will burn". Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ("quemará"), where it cannot take a capital, so there is no span there; the possessives "su" keep theirs.

decisions.choice: une fourche à vanner
decisions.reason: The tool is a wooden fork or shovel used to toss grain into the wind (m1). The traditional French "van" is a wide basket, a different tool. In Readable the farmer of the comparison ("où il sépare") takes no deity_pronoun span; the coming one does, as in the English.

decisions.choice: chombo cha kupepetea
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 3:12: a "pepeto" is the flat tray used to winnow by shaking; the Greek tool is a fork for tossing grain into the wind (meaning decision m1). "Chombo cha kupepetea" (winnowing tool) names its use without the wrong picture.

source.text: Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἕτερα παρακαλῶν εὐηγγελίζετο τὸν λαόν·

records.literal_gloss: Many indeed therefore and other things exhorting he was proclaiming good news to the people;

en.L: So with many other exhortations he was proclaiming the good news to the people.
en.B: With many other words of appeal, John announced the good news to the people.
en.R: John said many other things to urge the people to change, and he told them the good news.

es.L: Así que, con muchas otras exhortaciones, anunciaba la buena noticia al pueblo.
es.B: Con muchas otras palabras de exhortación, Juan anunciaba al pueblo la buena noticia.
es.R: Juan dijo muchas otras cosas para animar a la gente a cambiar, y le anunciaba la buena noticia.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, avec beaucoup d’autres exhortations, il annonçait la bonne nouvelle au peuple.
fr.B: C’est par bien d’autres appels encore que Jean annonçait la bonne nouvelle au peuple.
fr.R: Jean a dit encore beaucoup d’autres choses pour pousser les gens à changer de vie, et il leur a annoncé la bonne nouvelle.

sw.L: Basi akiwasihi kwa mambo mengine mengi, alikuwa akiwahubiria watu habari njema.
sw.B: Kwa maneno mengine mengi ya kuwasihi, Yohana aliwahubiria watu habari njema.
sw.R: Yohana alisema mambo mengine mengi kuwahimiza watu wabadilike, na aliwaambia habari njema.

decisions.choice: exhorting he proclaimed the good news: John's warnings were part of the good news
alternatives: the warnings and the good news were opposites
decisions.reason: The good news John announced is that the Lord is coming with salvation (3:6), which calls for repentance. The verb is the one used by the angels (1:19; 2:10).

decisions.choice: anunciaba la buena noticia
decisions.reason: The Greek verb names the act of announcing good news, and John's warnings belong to it (meaning decision m1). "La buena noticia" keeps that plain at every level; "el evangelio" is kept for places where the message itself is named.

decisions.choice: annoncer la bonne nouvelle, for the verb, at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "l’Évangile" for the noun at Literal and Balanced. Here Luke uses the verb, and French "évangéliser" now sounds like church jargon; "annoncer la bonne nouvelle" says what the verb means at every level, as the English does.

decisions.choice: habari njema
decisions.reason: The Greek verb names the act of announcing good news, and John's warnings belong to it (meaning decision m1). "Kuhubiri habari njema" says that at every level; "Injili" is kept for places where the message itself is named.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης, ἐλεγχόμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ περὶ Ἡρῳδιάδος τῆς γυναικὸς τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν πονηρῶν ὁ Ἡρῴδης, προσέθηκεν καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ πᾶσιν, καὶ κατέκλεισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν φυλακῇ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Herod the tetrarch, being rebuked by him concerning Herodias the wife of the brother of him and concerning all which did evils the Herod, \v 20 added also this upon all, and shut up the John in prison.

en.L: But Herod the tetrarch, being rebuked by him concerning Herodias, his brother's wife, and concerning all the evil things that Herod had done, \v 20 added this also to them all: he shut up John in prison.
en.B: But John had rebuked Herod the tetrarch for taking Herodias, his brother's wife, and for all the other evil things he had done. \v 20 So Herod added this to all the rest: he locked John up in prison.
en.R: John told Herod, the ruler of Galilee, that he was wrong to marry Herodias, his brother's wife. He also told Herod that the other evil things he had done were wrong. \v 20 Then Herod did something even worse. He put John in prison.

es.L: Pero Herodes el tetrarca, siendo reprendido por él a causa de Herodías, la mujer de su hermano, y a causa de todas las maldades que Herodes había hecho, \v 20 añadió también esto a todas ellas: encerró a Juan en prisión.
es.B: Pero Juan había reprendido al tetrarca Herodes por haber tomado a Herodías, la mujer de su hermano, y por todas las demás maldades que había cometido. \v 20 Y Herodes añadió a todo eso una más: encerró a Juan en la cárcel.
es.R: Juan le dijo a Herodes, el gobernante de Galilea, que había hecho mal al casarse con Herodías, la esposa de su hermano. También le dijo que las otras maldades que había hecho estaban mal. \v 20 Entonces Herodes hizo algo todavía peor: metió a Juan en la cárcel.

fr.L: Mais Hérode le tétrarque, repris par lui au sujet d’Hérodiade, la femme de son frère, et au sujet de toutes les mauvaises actions qu’Hérode avait commises, \v 20 ajouta encore ceci à tout le reste : il enferma Jean en prison.
fr.B: Mais Jean avait reproché à Hérode le tétrarque d’avoir pris Hérodiade, la femme de son frère, ainsi que toutes les autres mauvaises actions qu’il avait commises. \v 20 Alors Hérode ajouta encore ceci à tout le reste : il fit enfermer Jean en prison.
fr.R: Jean avait dit à Hérode, qui gouvernait la Galilée, qu’il avait eu tort d’épouser Hérodiade, la femme de son frère. Il lui avait dit aussi que les autres mauvaises choses qu’il avait faites étaient mal. \v 20 Alors Hérode a fait quelque chose de pire encore : il a mis Jean en prison.

sw.L: Lakini Herode mtawala, akikemewa naye kuhusu Herodia mke wa ndugu yake, na kuhusu maovu yote aliyokuwa ameyafanya Herode, \v 20 aliyaongezea yote hayo na hili pia: alimfungia Yohana gerezani.
sw.B: Lakini Yohana alikuwa amemkemea Herode mtawala kwa kumchukua Herodia, mke wa ndugu yake, na kwa maovu mengine yote aliyokuwa ametenda. \v 20 Kwa hiyo Herode akaongeza jambo hili kwenye mengine yote: akamtia Yohana gerezani.
sw.R: Yohana alimwambia Herode, mtawala wa Galilaya, kwamba alikosea kumwoa Herodia, mke wa ndugu yake. Alimwambia pia kwamba maovu mengine aliyofanya yalikuwa mabaya. \v 20 Kisha Herode alifanya jambo baya zaidi. Alimfunga Yohana gerezani.

decisions.choice: Herodias, his brother's wife: Herod Antipas married his half-brother's wife
decisions.reason: Herodias left her husband, a half-brother of Antipas, to marry Antipas. The law forbade marrying a brother's wife while the brother lived (Leviticus 18:16; 20:21; Mark 6:17-18).

decisions.choice: Luke tells of John's arrest before Jesus's baptism: he finishes John's story first
alternatives: John was arrested before he baptized Jesus
decisions.reason: John baptized Jesus (Mark 1:9), so the arrest came later. Luke sets it here to close John's part before turning to Jesus, as he did with Mary in 1:56.

decisions.choice: for taking Herodias (B); to marry Herodias (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the rebuke was about.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ βαπτισθῆναι ἅπαντα τὸν λαὸν καὶ Ἰησοῦ βαπτισθέντος καὶ προσευχομένου ἀνεῳχθῆναι τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ καταβῆναι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον σωματικῷ εἴδει ὡς περιστερὰν ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ φωνὴν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ γενέσθαι· Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.

records.literal_gloss: It came to pass and in the to be baptized all the people and Jesus having been baptized and praying was opened the heaven \v 22 and descended the Spirit the Holy in bodily form like a dove upon him, and a voice out of heaven came, You are the Son of me the beloved, in you I am well pleased.

en.L: And it happened, when all the people were baptized, and Jesus had been baptized and was praying, [that] heaven was opened \v 22 and the Holy Spirit came down upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came out of heaven: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved; in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I am well pleased."
en.B: At the time when all the people were being baptized, Jesus also received baptism. As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed, heaven opened, \v 22 and the Holy Spirit came down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in bodily form, like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear Son; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart delight."
en.R: Many people were being baptized, and Jesus was also baptized. While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying, the sky opened. \v 22 The Holy Spirit came down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The Spirit had a body that looked like a dove. Then a voice came from heaven. It said, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: Y sucedió, cuando todo el pueblo era bautizado, y Jesús había sido bautizado y estaba orando, [que] se abrió el cielo, \v 22 y descendió sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} el Espíritu Santo en forma corporal como una paloma, y vino una voz del cielo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo, el amado; en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} me complazco».
es.B: Cuando todo el pueblo se estaba bautizando, Jesús también fue bautizado. Mientras oraba, el cielo se abrió, \v 22 y el Espíritu Santo bajó sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en forma corporal, como una paloma. Y vino una voz del cielo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo querido; en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} se deleita {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón».
es.R: Mucha gente se estaba bautizando, y Jesús también fue bautizado. Mientras oraba, el cielo se abrió. \v 22 El Espíritu Santo bajó sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. El Espíritu tenía una forma que se podía ver, como una paloma. Entonces vino una voz del cielo, que dijo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo, y yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amo. Estoy muy contento contigo».

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand tout le peuple fut baptisé, et que Jésus, ayant été baptisé, priait, que le ciel s’ouvrit, \v 22 et que l’Esprit Saint descendit sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sous une forme corporelle, comme une colombe, et qu’une voix vint du ciel : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils, le bien-aimé ; en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} je prends plaisir. »
fr.B: Comme tout le peuple se faisait baptiser, Jésus aussi reçut le baptême. Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} priait, le ciel s’ouvrit, \v 22 et l’Esprit Saint descendit sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sous une forme corporelle, comme une colombe. Et une voix vint du ciel : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils bien-aimé ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais la joie de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur. »
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens se faisaient baptiser, et Jésus aussi a été baptisé. Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} priait, le ciel s’est ouvert. \v 22 L’Esprit Saint est descendu sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. L’Esprit avait un corps qui ressemblait à une colombe. Puis une voix est venue du ciel. Elle a dit : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils, et je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}aime. Je suis très content de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. »

sw.L: Ikawa, watu wote walipokuwa wakibatizwa, na Yesu akiwa amebatizwa na akiomba, mbingu zilifunguka, \v 22 na Roho Mtakatifu akashuka juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika umbo la mwili kama njiwa, na sauti ikaja kutoka mbinguni, "Wewe ndiwe Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, yule mpendwa; ndani {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} nimependezwa."
sw.B: Watu wote walipokuwa wakibatizwa, Yesu pia alibatizwa. Alipokuwa akiomba, mbingu zilifunguka, \v 22 na Roho Mtakatifu akashuka juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa umbo la mwili, kama njiwa. Kisha sauti ikasikika kutoka mbinguni: "Wewe ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mpendwa; {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unaufurahisha moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.R: Watu wengi walikuwa wakibatizwa, na Yesu pia alibatizwa. Alipokuwa akiomba, anga lilifunguka. \v 22 Roho Mtakatifu alishuka juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Roho alikuwa na umbo lililoonekana kama njiwa. Kisha sauti ikatoka mbinguni. Ilisema, "Wewe ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, nami nakupenda. Ninapendezwa sana {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}."

decisions.choice: Jesus baptized and praying: Luke tells of the baptism briefly and stresses the prayer
alternatives: the Spirit came during the baptism itself
decisions.reason: Luke mentions Jesus's baptism in passing and says the heavens opened while he was praying. Prayer marks the turning points of Jesus's life in Luke (6:12; 9:18, 28; 22:41).

decisions.choice: in bodily form like a dove: a visible form
alternatives: only a manner of gliding down
decisions.reason: Luke alone says "bodily form": the Spirit's coming could be seen. "Like a dove" compares the form; it does not say a bird appeared.

decisions.choice: You are my Son, the beloved; in you I am well pleased: Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1
decisions.reason: God says to his king, "You are my Son" (Psalm 2:7). Of his chosen servant he says that he delights in him and puts his Spirit on him (Isaiah 42:1). "Beloved" may recall Isaac, Abraham's only son (Genesis 22:2). Jesus is king, servant and Son.

decisions.choice: in you I am well pleased, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "today I have begotten you", the reading of one early Greek manuscript and several early writers
decisions.reason: Some witnesses give the rest of Psalm 2:7: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you." Most manuscripts have the reading of the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: I am well pleased: I take delight in you
alternatives: I have chosen you only now
decisions.reason: The aorist tense states God's settled delight in his Son, not a choice made at this moment.

decisions.choice: my dear Son; you bring my heart delight
alternatives: my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased
decisions.reason: "Well pleased" is weaker in modern English than the Greek. Balanced says what delight the Father takes in his Son.

decisions.choice: the sky (R); heaven (L, B)
decisions.reason: The same word means sky and heaven. Readable says the sky opened; the voice comes from heaven.

decisions.choice: le ciel at every level
alternatives: the sky / heaven distinction of the English Readable
decisions.reason: English Readable says "the sky" opened and the voice came from "heaven" because English has two words. French "le ciel" means both, so every level uses it, and the wording of the Father's voice follows Mark 1:11.

decisions.choice: about thirty years old when he began: when he began his public work
alternatives: when he began to be thirty
decisions.reason: "Beginning" stands alone in the Greek; Acts 1:22 and 10:37 speak of the beginning of Jesus's work after John's baptism. Thirty was the age when Joseph entered Pharaoh's service and David became king (Genesis 41:46; 2 Samuel 5:4).

decisions.choice: the son, as was supposed, of Joseph: Joseph was his legal father, not his natural father
alternatives: Luke doubts Joseph's fatherhood in general
decisions.reason: Luke has told of the virgin birth (1:34-35). People thought Jesus was Joseph's son (4:22); in law he was, and through Joseph he belongs to David's line.

decisions.choice: the son of Heli: each "of" means "son of"
decisions.reason: The Greek gives only the article "the" with each name, meaning "the son of". Matthew names Joseph's father as Jacob (Matthew 1:16). Some explain the difference by legal adoption or levirate marriage; others think Luke traces Mary's line through Heli, her father. The text itself does not say.

decisions.choice: the son of Adam, the son of God: the line goes back to the first man, made by God
decisions.reason: Matthew begins with Abraham and goes forward; Luke goes back past Abraham to Adam, so Jesus belongs to the whole human race. Adam is "of God" because God made him (Genesis 1:27; 2:7). The genealogy stands between the voice that calls Jesus God's Son (3:22) and the devil's "If you are the Son of God" (4:3).

decisions.choice: Nathan: a son of David, not the prophet
decisions.reason: Nathan was a son of David by Bathsheba (2 Samuel 5:14; 1 Chronicles 3:5). Matthew traces the line through Solomon, Luke through Nathan.

decisions.choice: Obed and Sala: the SBLGNT spells the names Iobel and Sala
alternatives: Obed and Salmon, as in Ruth 4:20-22 and many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have "Iobel" and "Sala" here; many later ones have the Old Testament spellings Obed and Salmon. The men are the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Admin, Arni: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Aram, the reading of many manuscripts, as in Ruth 4:19 and Matthew 1:3-4
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ widely here. The SBLGNT follows early manuscripts with two names, Admin and Arni; many have only "Aram". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Cainan: a name found in the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 11:12-13
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Genesis 11:12 and 1 Chronicles 1:24 has no Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah; the Greek Old Testament has him. Luke follows the Greek Old Testament.

decisions.choice: Joshua: the same name as Jesus
decisions.reason: The Greek name is Iesous, the form of Joshua used for Jesus himself. Here it is an ancestor.

decisions.choice: began his work
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what he began, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the usual English spellings of the names (Matthat, Joanan, Eber, ...)
decisions.reason: Names that appear in the Old Testament are given in their usual English form (Shealtiel, Hezron, Eber); the others are transliterated from the Greek.

decisions.choice: Here is Joseph's family line, all the way back to Adam, who came from God
decisions.reason: Readable introduces the long list and says where it ends.

decisions.choice: names in their usual Spanish Old Testament form: Zorobabel, Salatiel, Isaí, Booz, Naasón, Hezrón, Fares, Taré, Matusalén; the rest transliterated (Matat, Janay, Semeín, Josec, Jodá)
decisions.reason: As the English uses the Old Testament forms, so does the Spanish, as in Matthew 1, so readers can find these people in Genesis, Ruth and Chronicles. The names found only here are spelled simply from the Greek. Spanish Bibles differ on some spellings; a reviewer may settle them.

decisions.choice: comenzó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} obra (B, R); no span in Literal
decisions.reason: The English Literal has spans on "himself" and "he". Spanish says "Jesús mismo" (an adjective, which takes no span) and "al comenzar" with no pronoun, so Literal has none; Balanced and Readable keep the span on "su".

decisions.choice: the usual French forms of the names (Zorobabel, Salathiel, Booz, Jessé, Térah, Noé, Mathusalem, Hénoch); the others transliterated from the Greek
alternatives: the Greek forms throughout (Thara, Nachor, Ragaü, Phalek)
decisions.reason: As the English does, names that appear in the Old Testament are given in the form French readers know; the rest are transliterated. French Bibles differ on several of these (Nahshôn / Naasson, Hesron / Esrom, Pérès / Pharès, Térah / Thara), so a reviewer should settle them with the Old Testament and Matthew 1. "Josué" for the Greek name that is also Jesus's (m9).

decisions.choice: [fils] de ... at Literal
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats only the article, "the [one] of"; French cannot say "le d’Héli", so Literal supplies "fils" in brackets each time, as the English supplies "son" (m3).

decisions.choice: names in a Swahili Old Testament form: Zerubabeli, Shealtieli, Yese, Boazi, Nashoni, Hesroni, Peresi, Tera, Methusela; the rest adapted from the Greek (Mathati, Yanai, Semeini, Yoseki, Yoda)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 1, the names take their Old Testament form so readers can find these people in Genesis, Ruth and Chronicles; the names found only here are adapted simply from the Greek. Spellings vary between Swahili Bibles; a native reviewer should settle them for the whole genealogy.

decisions.choice: [mwana] wa
decisions.reason: Each link in the Greek is only "of" (meaning decision m3). Swahili could say "Yusufu wa Eli", but a long chain of bare "wa" is hard to follow, so Literal supplies "[mwana]" as the English supplies "[son]".
